experiences.name: Praia Dona Ana Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxing day at one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, just a short walk from Lagos town center. Praia Dona Ana features dramatic golden limestone cliffs, crystal-clear turquoise waters, and soft sand. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella, explore the sea caves by foot at low tide, and enjoy fresh seafood at the beachside restaurant.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Cheese Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided wine tasting session at a local Lagos wine bar near the historic center, sampling regional Algarve wines including Vida Nova rosé and Quinta dos Vales reds, paired with local cheeses and charcuterie. Learn about the unique terroir of the Algarve wine region from a knowledgeable sommelier.

experiences.name: Ponta da Piedade Kayak & Snorkel Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic sea caves and golden rock arches of Ponta da Piedade on a guided kayak tour departing from Lagos marina. Snorkel in hidden grottos and lagoons teeming with marine life, and witness breathtaking coastal scenery accessible only by water. A perfect blend of adventure and natural beauty.

experiences.name: Quinta dos Vales Vineyard Tour & Tasting
experiences.description: Take a half-day excursion to one of the Algarve's premier wineries, Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar. Enjoy a guided tour of the vineyards and wine cellar, followed by a tasting of five award-winning wines including their signature Marquês dos Vales Grande Reserva. The estate also features impressive outdoor sculptures and stunning countryside views.

experiences.name: Meia Praia Sunset Beach Walk & Seafood Dinner
experiences.description: Stroll along the vast 4km stretch of Meia Praia, a wide sandy beach just east of Lagos, during the golden hour for spectacular Atlantic sunset views. Afterward, dine at a local beachside restaurant serving freshly grilled fish, cataplana seafood stew, and local Algarve wines, combining the best of beach culture and regional cuisine.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Eva Bus or Rede Expressos coach from Faro Airport to Lagos (approx. €5-7, ~1.5 hours). Check in to Boutique Taghostel on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva. Freshen up and get settled.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a 24h petrol station near the bus terminal or a kebab shop near Lagos center (~€3-5)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Faro–Lagos bus ticket online at rede-expressos.pt to save time. The hostel is a short walk or cheap taxi (~€5) from Lagos bus station. Keep energy for tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy the hostel's communal area. Walk to the historic old town of Lagos — explore the 16th-century city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the charming cobblestone streets. Visit the free Igreja de Santo António exterior and the nearby Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos, ~€3 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia, a long golden beach just east of Lagos (15-min walk or free bike from hostel if available). Swim, relax, and soak up the September sun. The crowds thin out in mid-September making it ideal. Explore the rock formations at Ponta da Piedade on foot (30-min walk from town) — stunning golden cliffs and sea caves, completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Lagos marina at sunset. Enjoy the lively atmosphere of Rua 25 de Abril, Lagos's main bar street. Grab a cheap beer or glass of local Algarve wine at one of the outdoor terraces.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mulher de Capote near the hostel — coffee + pastel de nata for ~€2
meals.lunch: Grab a prego (steak sandwich) or bifana at a local tasca near the market for ~€4-5
meals.dinner: O Camilo or a local tasca on Rua do Ferrador — prato do dia (dish of the day) with wine for ~€8-10

day_by_day.notes: September weather in Algarve is warm (24-28°C) with minimal rain — perfect beach weather. Bring sunscreen and a reusable water bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus (EVA Bus line, ~€2.50) or rent a bicycle (~€10/day from Lagos bike shops) to Praia da Luz, a beautiful village beach 6km west of Lagos. Arrive early to enjoy the calm morning sea and dramatic red cliffs. Walk the coastal path along the cliffs for free panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue west by bus or bike to Burgau, a tiny whitewashed fishing village with a quiet beach. Explore the village, chat with locals, and enjoy the authentic Algarvian atmosphere. Return to Lagos by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Lagos Municipal Market (Mercado Municipal) area for a walk. Head to Rua 25 de Abril for the evening — many bars offer happy hour deals (2-for-1 cocktails, cheap wine). Try a glass of local Algarve wine such as Vida Nova or Quinta dos Vales.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen DIY or local padaria (bakery) — toast, coffee, juice for ~€2-3
meals.lunch: Fresh fish sandwich or grilled sardines at a beach snack bar in Praia da Luz for ~€6-8
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — grilled fish or cataplana for ~€10-12 with house wine

day_by_day.notes: Burgau is a hidden gem — far fewer tourists than Lagos. The coastal walk between Luz and Burgau is about 5km and takes ~1.5 hours if you choose to hike it.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres — take the EVA Bus from Lagos bus station (~€4.50 each way, ~1 hour). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry), a 15th-century fortress at the southwestern tip of Europe. Walk the clifftop paths with stunning Atlantic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or hitch to Praia do Beliche or Praia da Mareta in Sagres — wild, windswept beaches popular with surfers. Explore Cabo de São Vicente (Cape St. Vincent), the most southwestern point of continental Europe — free to visit, just €1 for the lighthouse museum. Watch the famous sunset here.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus. Relax at the hostel and socialize with fellow travelers. Join a hostel-organized pub crawl or social event if available.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and toast at the hostel or a café near the bus station for ~€2
meals.lunch: A Tasca in Sagres village — grilled fish of the day with salad and bread for ~€9-11
meals.dinner: Back in Lagos — Nah Nah Bah burger bar or a cheap pizza place on Rua 25 de Abril for ~€8-10

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is windier and cooler than Lagos — bring a light jacket. The last bus back to Lagos is around 19:30-20:00, so check the EVA timetable in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a kayak or join a budget group kayaking tour from Lagos marina (~€20-25 per person) to explore the famous sea caves and grottos at Ponta da Piedade. This is one of the most iconic experiences in the Algarve and well worth the splurge.
day_by_day.afternoon: After kayaking, relax at Praia do Camilo — a small, sheltered beach near Ponta da Piedade accessible via wooden stairs. Swim and sunbathe. Walk back to Lagos along the clifftop trail (free, ~45 minutes).
day_by_day.evening: Saturday night in Lagos is lively. Head to the marina area for sunset drinks, then explore the old town nightlife. Try a ginjinha (cherry liqueur) shot at a local bar for €1-2.

meals.breakfast: Café Golfinho near the marina — full Portuguese breakfast (eggs, toast, coffee) for ~€4-5
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach — buy bread, cheese, local presunto (ham), and fruit from the Mercado Municipal for ~€5
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon or a local tasca — try arroz de marisco (seafood rice) shared between two for ~€12-14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the kayak tour the day before as Saturday slots fill up quickly. Ponta da Piedade is best visited in the morning when the light is golden and the sea is calmer.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Silves — catch the train from Lagos station (~€3.50, ~40 minutes). Explore the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€2.80 entry), the best-preserved Moorish castle in Portugal. Walk the ancient walls for panoramic views over orange groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves old town — visit the Gothic Cathedral (free entry), stroll along the Arade River, and browse the Sunday market if running. Visit a local wine shop to pick up a bottle of Algarve wine for €4-6.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by train. Enjoy a quiet Sunday evening — cook a simple meal in the hostel kitchen with ingredients from the market, or join fellow travelers for a communal dinner.

meals.breakfast: On the train or grab a pastel de nata at Lagos station café for ~€1.50
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves — traditional Portuguese lunch with wine for ~€10-12
meals.dinner: Self-catered at the hostel — pasta, local cheese, and Algarve wine for ~€5-6 total

day_by_day.notes: Silves is the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve and far less touristy than Lagos. The train journey through orange and almond groves is scenic and relaxing.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Dona Ana, one of Lagos's most photogenic beaches, a 20-minute walk from the hostel. Arrive early to claim a spot among the golden rock formations. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the entire Lagos coastal cliff trail from Dona Ana to Ponta da Piedade and back (~3km each way, free). Stop at viewpoints for photos. Visit the small chapel at Ponta da Piedade. Return to town and visit the free Museu de Lagos (check for free Monday entry).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local wine scene — visit a wine bar in Lagos old town such as Vinha Bar or similar. Try a flight of Algarve wines (Vida Nova, Quinta dos Vales, Monte da Casteleja) for ~€8-10.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen or local padaria — coffee and croissant for ~€2
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Dona Ana — grilled chicken wrap or sandwich for ~€6-7
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celso or similar local restaurant — bacalhau à brás (codfish) with salad for ~€9-11

day_by_day.notes: Monday is quieter in Lagos — great day to visit popular spots without weekend crowds. The cliff walk is free and one of the most beautiful coastal walks in Portugal.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Portimão and Praia da Rocha — take the train from Lagos (~€2.50, 20 minutes). Praia da Rocha is a wide, dramatic beach with impressive rock formations. Walk the clifftop promenade for free views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Portimão town — visit the free Museu de Portimão (housed in a former sardine canning factory, free on Sundays, €3 other days). Walk along the Arade River waterfront. Browse the local market for fresh produce and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Visit the Lagos fish market area in the evening for a local experience. Enjoy a sunset drink at a rooftop bar or terrace overlooking the marina.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and toast at the hostel for ~€2
meals.lunch: Portimão is famous for grilled sardines — eat at a riverside tasca near the fish market for ~€8-10
meals.dinner: Back in Lagos — Restaurante Adega da Marina or similar for piri-piri chicken with fries for ~€9

day_by_day.notes: Portimão's sardine grilling tradition is legendary — if you see smoke rising from the riverside restaurants, follow it! The Museu de Portimão is genuinely excellent and budget-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Take a taxi or Uber (~€15-20 each way) or rent a bicycle to visit Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (about 25km from Lagos). Book a budget wine tour and tasting in advance (~€15-20 per person). Walk the vineyards and learn about Algarve wine production.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a second winery — Monte da Casteleja near Lagos is closer (~8km, cyclable). They offer informal tastings and sell bottles from €6-8. Buy a bottle or two to enjoy at the hostel. Return to Lagos by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the hostel with your wine purchases. Share bottles with fellow travelers in the communal area. Cook a simple dinner in the hostel kitchen.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at a local café near the hostel for ~€4-5
meals.lunch: Picnic at the winery or nearby — buy local cheese, bread, and charcuterie for ~€6-8
meals.dinner: Self-catered hostel dinner — local cheese, bread, olives, and wine for ~€6-8

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book winery visits as they may require reservations. Monte da Casteleja is the most accessible from Lagos and very welcoming to budget travelers. Algarve wines are underrated — bold reds and crisp whites.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the western Algarve — take the bus to Aljezur (~€4, 1 hour) in the Costa Vicentina Natural Park. Visit the ruined Moorish castle (free) with panoramic views. Walk through the charming whitewashed village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local taxi or hitch to Praia da Arrifana (~5km from Aljezur) — a spectacular wild beach backed by dramatic cliffs, popular with surfers. Swim or watch surfers. Walk the clifftop path for free views. Return to Aljezur and catch the bus back to Lagos.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Lagos, enjoy a relaxed evening. Visit the weekly market area or browse local craft shops. Have a final evening drink at a bar on Rua 25 de Abril.

meals.breakfast: Quick coffee and pastel de nata at Lagos bus station café for ~€2
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Praia da Arrifana — fresh fish sandwich or soup for ~€5-7
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Galeão in Lagos — traditional cataplana (seafood stew) for ~€12-14

day_by_day.notes: Arrifana is one of the most beautiful and unspoiled beaches in Portugal. The Costa Vicentina is a protected natural park — no overdevelopment, just raw Atlantic beauty.

day_by_day.morning: Revisit your favorite Lagos beach for a final relaxed morning swim. Try Meia Praia for its long stretch of sand and calm waters. Rent a paddleboard (~€10/hour) for a fun morning activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lagos old town in depth — visit the Igreja de Santa Maria (free), walk the old city walls, and browse the artisan shops on Rua Cândido dos Reis. Pick up budget souvenirs: local honey, almond sweets (Dom Rodrigo), or a bottle of medronho (arbutus berry spirit, ~€5-8).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Lagos — splurge slightly on a nicer restaurant. Try A Forja or Restaurante Casinha do Petisco for fresh seafood. Enjoy a final glass of Algarve wine and reflect on the trip.

meals.breakfast: Café Golfinho — full breakfast with fresh orange juice for ~€5
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a pastelaria — soup, bread, and coffee for ~€4-5
meals.dinner: Slightly splurge farewell dinner — grilled sea bass or lobster cataplana for ~€15-18 with wine

day_by_day.notes: Dom Rodrigo almond sweets are a traditional Algarve specialty and make great budget gifts. Medronho is the local firewater — try before you buy at a tasca.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — take a sunrise walk along the Lagos waterfront and marina. Visit the Mercado Municipal one last time for fresh fruit and pastries. Pack and check out of the hostel (store luggage if needed).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Meia Praia or Praia de Dona Ana for a final swim. Alternatively, take a free walking tour of Lagos old town (tip-based, ~€5-10 tip recommended) to learn the history of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Lagos bus station and take the EVA Bus to Faro Airport (~€7, ~1.5 hours) for any evening flights, or stay an extra night if your flight is the next day. Enjoy a final pastel de nata and coffee at the airport.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit and pastries from Mercado Municipal for ~€3-4
meals.lunch: Final prego sandwich or bifana at a local tasca for ~€4-5
meals.dinner: Airport café or pack snacks from the market for the journey home

day_by_day.notes: Check bus times to Faro Airport carefully — allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight departure. The EVA Bus is the cheapest option; a taxi costs ~€60-70.

day_by_day.morning: If still in Lagos — enjoy a slow Sunday morning. Visit the Sunday market near the waterfront for local produce, crafts, and antiques. Have a final long Portuguese breakfast at a café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final exploration of any missed spots — the Slave Market Museum, the old town walls, or a last swim at a nearby beach. Head to Lagos bus station for the transfer to Faro Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 days of stunning beaches, delicious seafood, excellent Algarve wines, and the warm hospitality of the Portuguese people.

meals.breakfast: Long leisurely breakfast at a local café — coffee, fresh orange juice, eggs, and toast for ~€5-6
meals.lunch: Sunday market snacks or a final tasca lunch for ~€8-10
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Total estimated budget for 13 days (excluding flights and accommodation): €400-550 per person, covering transport, meals, activities, and a few wine tastings. Lagos is one of the best value destinations in Western Europe — enjoy every moment!

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the airport shuttle or a pre-booked taxi (~50 min, ~€55) to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos. Check in, freshen up, and grab a light late-night snack near the hostel if anything is still open.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at a 24h petrol station convenience store or a late-closing kebab/pizza spot near Rua Dr. Faria e Silva if available

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – arrival is late. Pre-book your taxi or arrange an airport transfer in advance. Confirm check-in details with Taghostel as arrival is after 22:00. Pack light snacks in your carry-on for the journey.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, enjoy breakfast at the hostel or a nearby café. Take a gentle orientation walk through Lagos old town – explore the historic city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the charming cobblestone streets to get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia Dona Ana Beach (15-min walk from the hostel). Spend a relaxing afternoon at one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, surrounded by golden limestone cliffs and turquoise water. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella (~€10–12) and take a refreshing swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos town center. Stroll along the marina and watch the sunset over the water. Enjoy dinner at a traditional Portuguese restaurant in the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha or a local pastelaria near the hostel – pastel de nata, coffee, and fresh juice (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia Dona Ana – grilled fish sandwich, salad, and a cold Sagres beer (~€12–15)
meals.dinner: O Camilo Restaurant near Praia Dona Ana or Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos center – grilled sea bass or cataplana de marisco (~€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: September is still warm and sunny in the Algarve (avg 25–28°C). The sea is at its warmest this time of year. Praia Dona Ana can get busy – arrive by early afternoon for the best spot. Wear sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Book the Ponta da Piedade Kayak & Snorkel Tour (departs from Lagos marina, ~10 min walk from hostel). Paddle through the iconic sea caves, golden rock arches, and hidden grottos of Ponta da Piedade on a guided 3-hour tour. Snorkeling gear is typically included (~€35–45 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tour, dry off and head to the Mercado de Lagos (Lagos Municipal Market) for a browse of fresh local produce, cheeses, and cured meats. Pick up some local snacks. Rest at the hostel or relax at a café.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nightlife-friendly streets of Lagos. Visit a rooftop bar or a wine bar in the old town for pre-dinner drinks, then enjoy a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or Pastelaria Mira Mar near the center – toast, eggs, and coffee (~€6–8)
meals.lunch: Post-kayak lunch at Restaurante Bon Bom or a casual spot near the marina – prego sandwich or grilled sardines (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: No Pátio Restaurant in Lagos old town – Portuguese tapas and regional wines (~€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the kayak tour in advance online as September tours fill up quickly. Bring a change of clothes, water shoes if you have them, and a waterproof bag for your phone. The tour typically runs in the morning to avoid afternoon winds.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Algarve Wine & Cheese Tasting Experience at a local Lagos wine bar near the historic center. Sample regional wines from the Alentejo and Algarve DOC regions paired with local cheeses, chouriço, and presunto. A guided session typically lasts 1.5–2 hours (~€30–40 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk off the wine with a visit to the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos) and the Igreja de Santo António – both are within easy walking distance of the hostel and offer fascinating historical context (~€4–6 entry). Afterward, relax at a café with a bica (espresso).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Lagos marina waterfront for a sunset aperitivo. Enjoy dinner at a seafood-focused restaurant with marina views.

meals.breakfast: A Forja café near the hostel – fresh bread, butter, ham, and coffee (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Light lunch included or supplemented during the wine tasting, or grab a bifana (pork sandwich) from a local tasca (~€4–6)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Casinha do Petisco – traditional Algarvian cuisine, try the arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) (~€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the wine tasting experience in advance. September is harvest season in Portugal, making this an especially authentic time to taste local wines. Ask the sommelier about visiting a local quinta (winery) for a deeper experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente (westernmost point of continental Europe). Rent a car (~€30–40/day) or join a shared day tour from Lagos (~€25–35). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres and walk the clifftop trails with breathtaking Atlantic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Sagres area. Visit Praia do Beliche or Praia da Mareta for a swim in wilder, more rugged Atlantic waters. Browse the small surf shops and artisan stalls in Sagres village.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by early evening. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxed dinner in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hostel or a café before departure (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Restaurante O Telheiro do Infante in Sagres – fresh grilled fish with ocean views (~€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Taberna de Lagos – rustic Portuguese tavern with petiscos (small plates) and local wine (~€16–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Cabo de São Vicente can be windy even in September – bring a light jacket. The drive from Lagos to Sagres is about 35 minutes. Fuel up the rental car before returning. Saturday can be busy at Sagres – arrive early.

day_by_day.morning: Lazy Sunday morning – sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast. Visit the Lagos Sunday market (Mercado Municipal) if open, or browse the artisan craft stalls that often appear on weekends near the marina. Pick up local ceramics, cork products, or handmade jewelry as souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia – a long, wide sandy beach east of Lagos (10-min taxi or bike ride). This beach is less dramatic than Dona Ana but perfect for long walks, beach volleyball, and a more local crowd. Rent a paddleboard (~€15/hour) for some fun on the water.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a beach bar on Meia Praia, then head back to Lagos for dinner. Try a different neighborhood restaurant tonight.

meals.breakfast: Slow brunch at Café Paraíso in Lagos center – eggs, avocado toast, and fresh juice (~€9–12)
meals.lunch: Beach bar at Meia Praia – grilled chicken, salad, and a cold drink (~€12–15)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Mullens in Lagos – popular local spot with great grilled meats and fish (~€17–23 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Meia Praia is ideal for families and those wanting a calmer beach experience. The beach stretches for 4km so it rarely feels overcrowded. Bike rentals are available near the hostel (~€10–15/day) if you prefer cycling there.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves – the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Take a regional bus from Lagos bus station (~30 min, ~€3.50 each way) or drive. Visit the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves and the Gothic Sé Cathedral. Explore the charming town center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia in Silves to learn about the region's Moorish history. Walk along the Arade River and browse the local shops. If time allows, stop at a local quinta near Silves for an informal wine tasting – the area is known for its fig and citrus orchards.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by early evening. Enjoy a quiet dinner and an early night to recharge.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hostel before catching the bus (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves – famous for its seafood cataplana, a must-try (~€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: A Tasca do Celso in Lagos – cozy local restaurant with daily specials and affordable prices (~€14–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is one of the most historically rich towns in the Algarve and often overlooked by tourists. The castle entry is ~€3. September is a great time to visit as the summer crowds have thinned. Check bus schedules at Lagos bus terminal in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Praia Dona Ana for a second beach day, this time exploring the surrounding coves on foot. Walk the coastal path south from Lagos toward Ponta da Piedade – a stunning 2–3 km clifftop walk with panoramic views of the rock formations and sea stacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Ponta da Piedade lighthouse and viewpoint (free). Spend time photographing the dramatic landscape. Head back to Lagos and visit a local spa or wellness center for a relaxing massage (~€40–60 for 60 min) – well deserved mid-trip treat.
day_by_day.evening: Wine evening – visit a different wine bar in Lagos and try Alentejo reds and Vinho Verde whites. Pair with a cheese board.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local padaria (bakery) – fresh bread, cheese, and coffee (~€5–6)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the clifftops – pick up supplies from a local deli or supermarket (Pingo Doce nearby): local cheese, presunto, olives, bread, and fruit (~€8–10)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dom Sebastião in Lagos – upscale but mid-range, excellent cataplana and regional wines (~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The clifftop walk to Ponta da Piedade is moderately easy but wear proper footwear – some sections are uneven. The views are best in the late afternoon light. Book the spa in advance if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Portimão and Praia da Rocha. Take the train from Lagos station (~20 min, ~€2.50 each way) – one of the most scenic short rail journeys in Portugal. Explore Portimão's waterfront and the famous sardine grilling tradition along the riverside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Praia da Rocha – a wide, dramatic beach backed by ochre cliffs. Swim, sunbathe, and explore the rock formations at the western end of the beach. Visit the Fortaleza de Santa Catarina for free panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by train. Enjoy a final evening stroll along the Lagos marina before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café near Lagos train station – pastel de nata and galão coffee (~€4–5)
meals.lunch: Tasca da Dona Barca in Portimão – legendary grilled sardines on the riverside, a true Algarve experience (~€12–16 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos – reliable mid-range spot with great grilled fish and local wine (~€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Lagos–Portimão train runs regularly throughout the day. Portimão is famous for its sardine festival (usually August, but the tradition continues in September). Praia da Rocha is more developed and lively than Lagos beaches – good for a change of scenery.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a car and drive east to explore the quieter eastern Algarve. Head to Carrapateira and Praia da Bordeira – a wild, windswept beach in the Costa Vicentina Natural Park (~45 min drive). Walk the boardwalk trail through the dunes and estuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Aljezur – a charming hilltop village with a Moorish castle ruin. Browse the local market stalls and artisan shops. Visit Praia da Arrifana, a dramatic surf beach set in a natural amphitheater of cliffs (~15 min from Aljezur).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and pack for the next day's activities.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hostel before picking up the rental car (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Sitio do Rio in Carrapateira – rustic local restaurant with fresh fish and stunning views (~€14–18 per person)
meals.dinner: O Camilo Restaurant in Lagos – fresh seafood with cliff views, book ahead (~€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Costa Vicentina is a protected natural park – one of the last wild coastlines in Western Europe. Roads can be narrow and winding. Fill up the rental car before heading into the park. This area is popular with surfers and nature lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in Lagos. Visit the Farmers' Market or browse the local shops for last-minute souvenirs – look for local honey, fig jam, medronho (arbutus berry spirit), and handmade ceramics. Take a final walk along the city walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Book a sunset boat trip from Lagos marina – a 2-hour cruise along the Ponta da Piedade coastline, often including a stop for swimming in a sea cave (~€30–40 per person). This is a wonderful way to see the rock formations from the water one last time.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Lagos's best restaurants. Splurge slightly on a special meal to celebrate the trip.

meals.breakfast: Slow brunch at Café Ginginha or Pastelaria Mira Mar – full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, toast, cheese, and coffee (~€8–10)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a tapas bar in the old town – petiscos and a glass of wine (~€12–15)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dom Sebastião or Casinha do Petisco – order the house specialty and a bottle of local Alentejo red to celebrate (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sunset boat trips are very popular – book at least 2 days in advance. The golden hour light on the Ponta da Piedade cliffs from the water is absolutely spectacular. Bring a light layer as it can get breezy on the water in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning at Praia do Camilo – a small, secluded cove near Ponta da Piedade accessible via a wooden staircase down the cliffs. One of the most photogenic beaches in the Algarve. Arrive early to secure a spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for a final afternoon. Visit any remaining sights – the Museu Municipal de Lagos (~€3), or simply sit at a café in Praça Gil Eanes and people-watch. Do any final packing and check out logistics.
day_by_day.evening: Last evening in Lagos. Enjoy a casual dinner with fellow travelers or new friends made at the hostel. Visit a local bar for a farewell drink – try a ginjinha (cherry liqueur) or a glass of port.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local café – keep it light (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a local tasca – prego no pão (steak sandwich) or a simple grilled fish (~€10–13)
meals.dinner: Taberna de Lagos or No Pátio – relaxed, affordable farewell dinner with local wine (~€16–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Praia do Camilo has limited space – arrive before 10am on weekends. The wooden staircase has about 200 steps. Check hostel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your flight is the next day. Confirm taxi or transfer to Faro Airport.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Algarve. Enjoy a slow breakfast at a favorite café. Take one last walk along the Lagos waterfront or through the old town. Pick up any final souvenirs – a bottle of local wine, medronho, or Algarve sea salt make great gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, arrange a taxi or transfer to Faro Airport (~50 min, ~€55). Allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Reflect on 13 wonderful days in the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry the memories of golden cliffs, turquoise waters, and excellent Portuguese wine home with you.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and bica at a Lagos café – a perfect last taste of Portugal (~€4–5)
meals.lunch: Light meal at Faro Airport or a café near the airport (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer the night before to avoid stress on departure day. Faro Airport is small but can get busy on Sunday afternoons – arrive with plenty of time. Double-check passport, boarding pass, and any duty-free purchases. Obrigado e boa viagem – thank you and safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

experiences.name: Praia Dona Ana Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxing day at one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, just a short walk from Lagos town center. Praia Dona Ana features dramatic golden limestone cliffs, crystal-clear turquoise waters, and soft sand. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella, explore the sea caves by foot at low tide, and enjoy fresh seafood at the beachside restaurant.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Cheese Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided wine tasting session at a local Lagos wine bar near the historic center, sampling regional Algarve wines including Vida Nova rosé and Quinta dos Vales reds, paired with local cheeses and charcuterie. Learn about the unique terroir of the Algarve wine region from a knowledgeable sommelier.

experiences.name: Ponta da Piedade Kayak & Snorkel Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic sea caves and golden rock arches of Ponta da Piedade on a guided kayak tour departing from Lagos marina. Snorkel in hidden grottos and lagoons teeming with marine life, and witness breathtaking coastal scenery accessible only by water. A perfect blend of adventure and natural beauty.

experiences.name: Quinta dos Vales Vineyard Tour & Tasting
experiences.description: Take a half-day excursion to one of the Algarve's premier wineries, Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar. Enjoy a guided tour of the vineyards and wine cellar, followed by a tasting of five award-winning wines including their signature Marquês dos Vales Grande Reserva. The estate also features impressive outdoor sculptures and stunning countryside views.

experiences.name: Meia Praia Sunset Beach Walk & Seafood Dinner
experiences.description: Stroll along the vast 4km stretch of Meia Praia, a wide sandy beach just east of Lagos, during the golden hour for spectacular Atlantic sunset views. Afterward, dine at a local beachside restaurant serving freshly grilled fish, cataplana seafood stew, and local Algarve wines, combining the best of beach culture and regional cuisine.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer pre-arranged to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos (~1 hour drive). Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome glass of local Algarve wine at the hotel's lounge bar before retiring for the night.

meals.breakfast: On flight
meals.lunch: On flight or at airport
meals.dinner: Light late-night charcuterie and cheese board with a glass of Alentejo red wine at the hotel lounge upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private chauffeur transfer from Faro Airport to Lagos for a seamless luxury arrival. Confirm hotel late check-in in advance. Keep Day 1 light – rest is the priority.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the hotel, then a gentle orientation walk through Lagos' historic old town – explore the 16th-century city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the charming cobblestone streets. Visit the Igreja de Santo António, a stunning baroque church.
day_by_day.afternoon: Praia Dona Ana Beach Day – Head to one of the Algarve's most iconic beaches, just a short walk from the hotel. Settle into a premium sun lounger, swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters, and admire the dramatic golden limestone cliffs and sea stacks. Arrange a private beach butler service if available.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar overlooking the Atlantic, followed by a premium seafood dinner at a top Lagos restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at the hotel – fresh pastéis de nata, local cheeses, presunto, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside restaurant at Praia Dona Ana – grilled sea bass, fresh salads, and chilled Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Adega da Marina or No Pátio – indulge in cataplana de marisco (seafood stew), grilled lobster, and a bottle of premium Algarve white wine

day_by_day.notes: Praia Dona Ana is a short 10-minute walk from the hotel. September weather in the Algarve is typically warm (24–28°C) with calm seas – ideal beach conditions. Bring reef shoes as the beach has some rocky areas.

day_by_day.morning: Ponta da Piedade Kayak & Snorkel Tour – Embark on a guided luxury kayak tour through the world-famous sea caves, golden rock arches, and hidden grottos of Ponta da Piedade. Snorkel in the emerald waters and explore sea caves accessible only by kayak. A truly unmissable Algarve experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a relaxing afternoon. Enjoy a spa treatment or massage at the hotel or a nearby luxury wellness center. Alternatively, explore the Lagos Marina and browse the boutique shops along the waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Algarve Wine & Cheese Tasting Experience – Join an intimate guided wine tasting session at a curated Lagos wine bar near the historic center. Sample regional Algarve wines including Negra Mole reds and Arinto whites, paired with artisan local cheeses, smoked meats, and fig preserves.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – açorda (bread soup), fresh orange juice, local honey, and artisan pastries
meals.lunch: Post-kayak lunch at a waterfront restaurant in Lagos – grilled octopus salad, amêijoas à Bulhão Pato (clams), and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Light tapas-style dinner included as part of the wine and cheese tasting experience, supplemented by a post-tasting dinner at a nearby bistro if desired

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ponta da Piedade kayak tour in advance – small group or private tour recommended for a premium experience. Wear water shoes and bring a waterproof camera. The wine tasting typically lasts 2–2.5 hours and is best enjoyed on an empty stomach.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to Quinta dos Vales Vineyard near Estômbar (~30 minutes from Lagos). Enjoy a guided tour of the estate's vineyards, wine cellar, and sculpture garden. Participate in a premium tasting of their award-winning wines including Marquês dos Vales Grande Reserva.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the vineyard experience with a gourmet lunch on the estate terrace, then return to Lagos in the early afternoon. Spend the rest of the afternoon relaxing at the hotel pool or exploring the Mercado de Lagos for local artisan products.
day_by_day.evening: Meia Praia Sunset Beach Walk & Seafood Dinner – Take a private taxi or rideshare to Meia Praia (10 minutes east of Lagos). Stroll along the vast 4km golden beach as the sun sets over the Atlantic, then enjoy a premium seafood dinner at a beachside restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure to the vineyard
meals.lunch: Gourmet estate lunch at Quinta dos Vales – paired with their finest wines, featuring regional Algarve cuisine with seasonal ingredients
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at Meia Praia – whole grilled turbot, percebes (barnacles), and a bottle of premium Algarve Antão Vaz white wine

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private transport to Quinta dos Vales for the most comfortable experience. The vineyard tour and tasting typically lasts 3–4 hours. Meia Praia is best visited in the late afternoon for the golden hour light – bring a light jacket as evenings can be breezy by the sea.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a luxury convertible or hire a private driver for a scenic coastal drive along the Algarve's western coast. Visit the dramatic Praia do Camilo (a short walk from Lagos) and the wild, windswept Praia do Castelejo near Vila do Bispo. Explore the rugged Costa Vicentina landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Sagres and the iconic Fortaleza de Sagres – a 15th-century fortress at the southwestern tip of Europe. Explore the windswept promontory, the giant wind compass (Rosa dos Ventos), and enjoy panoramic Atlantic views. Stop at Cabo de São Vicente, Europe's most southwesterly point.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a refined dinner at one of the town's top restaurants. Enjoy the vibrant Saturday evening atmosphere in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with fresh local produce
meals.lunch: Lunch at a clifftop restaurant in Sagres – fresh tuna steak, local bread, and a glass of crisp Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Casinha do Petisco or A Forja in Lagos – traditional Portuguese cuisine elevated with premium ingredients, paired with an Alentejo Pêra-Manca red

day_by_day.notes: The western Algarve coast can be windier than the central/eastern Algarve – bring a light layer. Sagres is approximately 35 km from Lagos (40-minute drive). The fortress is a UNESCO-listed site and one of Portugal's most historically significant landmarks.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed Sunday morning – sleep in and enjoy a long, leisurely hotel breakfast. Spend the morning at the hotel pool or take a gentle yoga session if offered. Browse the Lagos Sunday market for local crafts, fresh produce, and artisan goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat charter from Lagos Marina – spend the afternoon cruising along the stunning Algarve coastline, visiting hidden sea caves, secluded beaches, and snorkeling spots inaccessible by land. Enjoy champagne and canapés on deck.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the marina at sunset. Enjoy pre-dinner drinks at a marina-side bar, then a premium dinner at a Lagos fine dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast – full spread with local specialties, fresh juices, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch served on the private boat – charcuterie, fresh seafood, local cheeses, fruit, and chilled Champagne
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bon Vivant Restaurant & Lounge in Lagos – creative Portuguese fine dining with an excellent wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter at least 2–3 days in advance. A 4–6 hour charter is ideal. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a light layer for the sea breeze. September seas are typically calm and ideal for boating.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves – the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve (~40 minutes from Lagos). Visit the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves, one of Portugal's best-preserved Moorish castles. Explore the charming town, the Gothic cathedral, and the riverside promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local artisan cork workshop or pottery studio in Silves. Then stop at a traditional tasca for a mid-afternoon snack before returning to Lagos. Alternatively, visit the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Lagos – explore the vibrant Rua 25 de Abril bar street for pre-dinner cocktails, then enjoy a premium dinner back at the hotel or a nearby restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves – one of the Algarve's most celebrated seafood restaurants, famous for its cataplana and grilled fish
meals.dinner: Dinner at the hotel restaurant or a nearby Lagos fine dining spot – grilled black pork (porco preto) with migas and a glass of Douro red

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a 40-minute drive from Lagos. Hire a private driver or rent a car. The castle is open daily and entry is affordable. Marisqueira Rui is extremely popular – book a table in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Praia Dona Ana or explore nearby Praia do Pinhão (a smaller, more secluded cove adjacent to Dona Ana). Spend a peaceful morning swimming, sunbathing, and reading on the golden sands. Hire a private beach cabana if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Paddleboard or stand-up kayak rental along the Lagos coastline. Alternatively, take a guided cliff-top walk from Ponta da Piedade back toward Lagos for spectacular aerial views of the sea caves and rock formations.
day_by_day.evening: Private wine pairing dinner experience – arrange a curated in-hotel or private villa dinner with a sommelier presenting a flight of premium Portuguese wines (Douro, Alentejo, Dão) paired with a multi-course tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at a premium beach club – grilled prawns, fresh salads, and a bottle of chilled Alvarinho
meals.dinner: Private multi-course wine pairing dinner – amuse-bouche, cured fish, slow-roasted lamb, artisan cheeses, and pastel de nata soufflé, paired with 5 premium Portuguese wines

day_by_day.notes: The private wine pairing dinner should be arranged 2–3 days in advance through the hotel concierge. This is a highlight experience for wine enthusiasts. The cliff-top walk from Ponta da Piedade is approximately 2 km and takes about 45 minutes at a leisurely pace.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Portimão and Praia da Rocha (~25 minutes from Lagos). Explore the vibrant Portimão waterfront, visit the Museu de Portimão (a fascinating former sardine canning factory turned museum), and stroll along the impressive Praia da Rocha beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the dramatic rock formations and sea caves at Praia da Rocha. Take a short boat trip from the beach to explore the caves up close. Browse the upscale boutiques and galleries along the Portimão marina.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Portimão at one of the city's top seafood restaurants, then return to Lagos by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at Taberna da Maré in Portimão – fresh grilled sardines, açorda de marisco, and local wines
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Titanic in Portimão – a long-standing Algarve institution known for exceptional seafood and traditional Portuguese cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Portimão is approximately 25 km from Lagos. The Museu de Portimão is free on Sunday afternoons and has excellent exhibits on the region's fishing heritage. Book the evening restaurant in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Guided cultural walking tour of Lagos with a private local historian guide. Discover the city's fascinating history as a major port in the Age of Discovery, visit the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos), the Igreja de Santa Maria, and the old city walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cooking class experience – join a premium Portuguese cooking class in Lagos, learning to prepare traditional Algarve dishes such as cataplana de marisco, amêijoas à Bulhão Pato, and pastel de nata. Enjoy your creations for lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar or clifftop terrace in Lagos, followed by a relaxed dinner at a wine bar with an extensive Portuguese wine list.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes prepared during the cooking class – a hands-on, delicious midday meal with wine pairings
meals.dinner: Dinner at Vinha Bar & Wine in Lagos – an intimate wine bar with an exceptional selection of natural and premium Portuguese wines, paired with small plates

day_by_day.notes: Book the private walking tour and cooking class through the hotel concierge. The Slave Market Museum is a sobering but important historical site – one of the oldest in Europe. The cooking class typically lasts 3–4 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Monchique – the lush mountain village in the Serra de Monchique (~1 hour from Lagos). Hike through eucalyptus and cork oak forests to the summit of Fóia (902m), the highest point in the Algarve, for panoramic views stretching to the Atlantic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the charming village of Monchique, explore the ruins of the Franciscan convent, and sample the local medronho (arbutus berry spirit) and smoked presunto at a traditional tasca. Visit the thermal spa town of Caldas de Monchique for a relaxing soak.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a final Friday evening celebration dinner at the best restaurant in town.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Central in Monchique – traditional mountain cuisine featuring roasted kid (cabrito), smoked meats, and local vegetables
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Restaurante Dom Sebastião in Lagos – one of the Algarve's finest restaurants, known for exceptional Portuguese cuisine and an award-winning wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Hire a private driver for the Monchique excursion – the mountain roads are winding and a driver allows you to fully enjoy the scenery. The thermal baths at Caldas de Monchique are a wonderful way to relax after the hike. Book Dom Sebastião well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning – return to your favorite Algarve beach (Praia Dona Ana, Praia do Camilo, or Meia Praia) for a last luxurious morning by the sea. Swim, sunbathe, and soak in the stunning scenery one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon for shopping and souvenir hunting in Lagos old town. Visit artisan shops for hand-painted azulejo tiles, local cork products, artisan ceramics, and bottles of premium Algarve wine and medronho to take home. Enjoy a final afternoon coffee and pastel de nata at a historic café.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner – a grand final evening at a premium Lagos restaurant or a private chef experience arranged at the hotel. Celebrate the end of an extraordinary Algarve journey with the finest Portuguese wines and cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Final beachside lunch – grilled fish of the day, fresh salad, and a last glass of chilled Alvarinho
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Restaurante Dom Sebastião or a private chef dinner at the hotel – multi-course tasting menu with wine pairings, featuring the best of Algarve and Portuguese cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Pack souvenirs carefully – wine bottles require protective packaging. Consider shipping larger purchases home. Confirm checkout time and arrange airport transfer for the following day if departing on Day 13.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely hotel breakfast. Check out of Boutique Taghostel. Take a last stroll through Lagos old town or along the marina promenade. Enjoy a final espresso at a local café and soak in the Algarve atmosphere one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time – either relax at the hotel (request late checkout if available) or head to the airport. Private luxury transfer from Lagos to Faro Airport (~1 hour). Allow ample time for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of beaches, wine, culture, and the unparalleled beauty of Portugal's Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast – savor every last bite of fresh pastéis de nata, local cheese, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel or a nearby café before departure, or at Faro Airport
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request a late checkout from the hotel to maximize your final morning in Lagos. Faro Airport is approximately 70 km from Lagos – allow at least 1.5 hours travel time plus 2 hours for airport procedures for international flights.
